'''Douglas Brent West''' is a [[professor]] of [[graph theory]] at [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]]. He received his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D]]. from [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1978; his advisor was [[Daniel Kleitman]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=4840|title=Douglas Brent West}}</ref> He is the "W" in [[G. W. Peck]], a [[pseudonym]] for a group of six [[Mathematician|mathematicians]] that includes West.<ref name="kcc">{{citation
 | last = Peck | first = G. W.
 | doi = 10.1016/S0012-365X(02)00595-2
 | mr = 1935723
 | issue = 2–3
 | journal = [[Discrete Mathematics (journal)|Discrete Mathematics]]
 | pages = 193–224
 | title = Kleitman and combinatorics: a celebration
 | volume = 257
 | year = 2002| doi-access = 
 }}.</ref> He is the editor of the journal ''[[Discrete Mathematics (journal)|Discrete Mathematics]]''.

==Selected work==

===Books===
* ''Introduction to Graph Theory'' - Second edition, Douglas B. West. Published by Prentice Hall 1996, 2001. {{isbn|0-13-014400-2}}
* ''Mathematical Thinking: Problem-Solving and Proofs'' Second edition, John P D'Angelo and Douglas West.  Published by Prentice Hall 1999.  {{isbn|0-13-014412-6}}
* ''Combinatorial Mathematics'' Douglas B. West. Published by Cambridge University Press 2020. {{isbn|1-107-05858-9}}

===Research work===
* Spanning trees with many leaves, [[Daniel Kleitman|DJ Kleitman]], DB West - [[SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics]], 1991.
* Class of Solutions to the Gossip Problem, Part II, DB West - Discrete Mathematics, 1982.
* The interval number of a planar graph: three intervals suffice, [[Ed Scheinerman|ER Scheinerman]], DB West - Journal of combinatorial theory. Series B, 1983.
